problem_text:
A logistics company needs to coordinate 7 delivery trucks across 7 distribution centers.

Each truck follows a predetermined route represented as pairs (Distribution Center, Unloading time),
where each pair specifies the distribution center where the truck must stop and the time required to unload its cargo.
The order of pairs indicates the required sequence in which the stops must be made.

Truck schedules:
* Truck 1 follows the route: (DC4, 4) → (DC1, 7) → (DC6, 4) → (DC2, 6) → (DC5, 3) → (DC7, 3) → (DC3, 8)
* Truck 2 follows the route: (DC6, 1) → (DC2, 7) → (DC5, 10) → (DC4, 1) → (DC3, 3) → (DC1, 9) → (DC7, 2)
* Truck 3 follows the route: (DC4, 3) → (DC3, 6) → (DC6, 5) → (DC2, 8) → (DC5, 8) → (DC1, 10) → (DC7, 6)
* Truck 4 follows the route: (DC3, 9) → (DC6, 7) → (DC1, 10) → (DC4, 8) → (DC5, 7) → (DC7, 3) → (DC2, 10)
* Truck 5 follows the route: (DC4, 2) → (DC2, 7) → (DC1, 5) → (DC5, 5) → (DC7, 2) → (DC6, 6) → (DC3, 9)
* Truck 6 follows the route: (DC7, 2) → (DC5, 7) → (DC1, 7) → (DC6, 8) → (DC4, 1) → (DC3, 6) → (DC2, 3)
* Truck 7 follows the route: (DC1, 1) → (DC6, 1) → (DC4, 10) → (DC2, 7) → (DC7, 3) → (DC3, 9) → (DC5, 5)

Each unloading operation must be completed without interruption once it begins,
and each distribution center can only accommodate one truck at a time for unloading.
The objective is to determine the scheduling sequence for all unloading operations at the distribution centers
so that the total completion time for all delivery routes is minimized.
